# Campfire in Rust

A Rust implementation of [ONCE Campfire](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire). It uses the
existing SQLite database, storage layout and signed/encrypted cookies, so existing installs can
upgrade without migrating data or signing everyone out.

One `campfire` executable replaces Ruby, Puma, Redis, Resque and Thruster, with libvips and ffmpeg
for media. The app includes TLS, HTTP/2, Web Push, search and Action Cable-compatible WebSockets.

## Running it

With [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once), on a server with Docker:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire-rust --host chat.example.com
```

ONCE manages secrets, TLS, backups and upgrades. Or run Docker directly:

```sh
docker run -d -p 80:80 -p 443:443 \
  -e SECRET_KEY_BASE=... -e VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=... -e VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=... \
  -e TLS_DOMAIN=chat.example.com \
  -v campfire:/rails/storage \
  ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire-rust
```

- `TLS_DOMAIN` enables automatic Let's Encrypt certificates; `DISABLE_SSL` enables plain HTTP.
- `/rails/storage` holds the database, uploads, backups and certificates. Existing installs must
  keep their storage and secrets.
- Web Push needs a valid P-256 VAPID key pair in URL-safe Base64. `VAPID_SUBJECT` sets the contact
  URL; its default is `https://` plus the first `TLS_DOMAIN`, or the project's URL.
- The app listener on `TARGET_PORT` (3000) binds loopback. `TARGET_BIND` overrides this; that listener
  trusts `X-Forwarded-*` from whoever reaches it. Other settings are in
  [`config.rs`](crates/campfire/src/config.rs).
- Images support amd64 and arm64. `:latest` and version tags track
  [releases](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire-rust/releases); `:main` tracks the main branch.

## Performance

Production image and seed data on four pinned hardware threads of an AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395:
medians of three runs on October 1, 2026, at
[`1ea6d6f`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire-rust/commit/1ea6d6f6b24fd21e7d01e69b7c92df5c380bcbde).
The [full report](bench/results/emoon-pr43-production-20261001/report.md) records settings and
ranges, and `bench/run` reproduces it.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Room page, 16 clients | 36,120 req/s |
| Messages page, 16 clients | 41,352 req/s |
| Sidebar, 16 clients | 34,339 req/s |
| Search, 16 clients | 33,510 req/s |
| Post a message, 16 clients | 6,817 req/s |
| `/up`, 16 clients | 233,085 req/s |
| Room page p99, 64 clients | 3.1 ms |
| Post a message p99, 64 clients | 13.9 ms |
| Upload a 505 KB JPEG until its thumbnail is served | 27.6 ms |
| Deliveries per second, 10,000 clients in one room | 671,674 |
| Post to all 10,000 clients received, p50 / p99 | 39.6 ms / 61.1 ms |
| Connect and subscribe 10,000 clients | 1.4 s |
| Cold start until `/up` answers | 157 ms |
| Idle memory (container, including page cache) | 20 MB |
| App memory, 10,000 clients under load (Pss) | 248 MB |
| Image size, unpacked / compressed download | 168 MB / 67 MB |

Daniel Collin ([emoon](https://github.com/emoon)) in
[#43](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire-rust/pull/43).

```sh

bin/dev        # http://localhost:3000
```

# Bots

Bots are chat members that post via an HTTP API (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages`).

## Data model

- `bots` table (Rust-only addition, created via `schema::ADDITIONS` so existing
  Rails databases gain it on boot):
  - `id`, `user_id UNIQUE` (the bot's `users` row, which carries name/avatar and
    memberships), `creator_id` (the human who created it), `bot_code UNIQUE`
    (the credential), timestamps.
- A bot's `users` row has no email and an empty `password_digest` (never used for
  password auth); it is `active`/`member` so existing queries (`User::active`,
  `grant_to_active_users`, room member lists) treat it like a person.
- Deleting a bot removes its `bots` row, its `users` row's avatar attachment, its
  memberships and sessions/push data is N/A; the `users` row itself is kept when it
  has messages (so history still renders) but marked deactivated? See controller.
  Simpler: keep the user row, delete only the `bots` row + memberships. Posting
  then 401s because the code is gone, while past messages still resolve their
  creator.

Actually implemented: `Bot::destroy` deletes the `bots` row, the bot user's
memberships, its avatar attachment (purge later), and — when the bot has no
messages — its `users` row as well. When messages exist the user row is kept so
`message.creator` still renders (presenter falls back to Unrenderable otherwise,
but keeping the row preserves name/avatar).

## Auth

- UI (`/bots*`) uses the normal session + `require_authentication`.
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` skips session/forgery, authenticates
  by `bot_code` (401 when unknown), 404 when the room is missing. The raw request
  body (`request.raw_post`) is the message body; empty (blank) with no attachment
  is 422. The message is created as `creator = bot.user_id` via `Message::create`
  + `canonical_body`, then `broadcast_create` (same as human `messages#create`),
  which also enqueues the push job via `Room::receive`.
